access.template: Client authentication for the proxy API. These are not upstream provider keys.

access.api-keys.description: APIKeys is a list of keys for authenticating clients to this proxy server.

access.key-allowlist.description:
KeyAllowlist restricts each client key to the upstream credentials it may
use. While it has any entry, a client key without one selects nothing.

access.key-allowlist[].api-key.description: APIKey is the client key, as listed in access.api-keys.

access.key-allowlist[].credentials.description: Credentials lists the rules a credential must match one of.

access.key-allowlist[].credentials[].acc.description:
Accounts, when set, narrows the rule to OAuth account emails returned by
AccountInfo, trimmed and compared case-sensitively. Empty emails never match.

access.key-allowlist[].credentials[].bas.description:
BaseURLs, when set, narrows the rule to API-key credentials whose
base-url is one of these, compared as CPA stores it (trimmed, otherwise
exact). It never matches an OAuth login or a credential without a base-url.

access.key-allowlist[].credentials[].ids.description:
IDs, when set, narrows the rule to these credential IDs; an OAuth login's
ID is its file path relative to the auth directory.

access.key-allowlist[].credentials[].kin.description: Kind is the credential kind, oauth or apikey. A rule with any other kind matches nothing.

access.key-allowlist[].credentials[].pro.description:
Provider is the credential's provider as CPA records it, such as claude,
codex or gemini, and openai-compatible-<name> for an openai-compatibility group.

api-keys.claude.description: ClaudeKey defines a list of Claude API key configurations as specified in the YAML configuration file.

api-keys.claude[].base-url.description:
BaseURL is the base URL for the Claude API endpoint.
If empty, the default Claude API URL will be used.

api-keys.claude[].disable-cooling.description:
DisableCooling overrides the global cooling policy for this credential when set.
True disables auth/model cooldowns; false explicitly enables them.

api-keys.claude[].excluded-models.description: ExcludedModels lists model IDs that should be excluded for this provider.

api-keys.claude[].headers.description: Headers optionally adds extra HTTP headers for requests sent with this key.

api-keys.claude[].keys[].api-key.description: APIKey is the authentication key for accessing Claude API services.

api-keys.claude[].keys[].cloak.description: Cloak configures request cloaking for non-Claude-Code clients.

api-keys.claude[].keys[].cloak.cache-use.description:
CacheUserID controls whether Claude user_id values are cached per API key.
When false, a fresh random user_id is generated for every request.

api-keys.claude[].keys[].cloak.mode.description:
Mode controls cloaking behavior: "auto" (default), "always", "never", or "uncloak".
Supplying this CloakConfig explicitly enables cloaking for an unprofiled API key.
- "auto": cloak unless strong request signals identify a verified native entrypoint
- "always": cloak every unconfirmed client; confirmed native Claude Code remains passthrough
- "never" / "uncloak": never apply cloaking; on non-CLI API keys, also strip incoming Claude Code identity and billing attribution

api-keys.claude[].keys[].cloak.sensitive.description:
SensitiveWords is a list of words to obfuscate with zero-width characters.
This can help bypass certain content filters.

api-keys.claude[].keys[].cloak.strict-mo.description:
StrictMode controls how caller system prompts are handled when cloaking.
- false (default): legacy-model whitelist uses a user reminder; all other models use a mid-conversation system message
- true: strip caller system prompts and keep only the Claude Code billing and identity blocks

api-keys.claude[].keys[].disable-cooling.description:
DisableCooling overrides the global cooling policy for this credential when set.
True disables auth/model cooldowns; false explicitly enables them.

api-keys.claude[].keys[].excluded-models.description: ExcludedModels lists model IDs that should be excluded for this provider.

api-keys.claude[].keys[].experimental-cc.description:
ExperimentalCCHSigning is retained for configuration compatibility.
CCH signing is automatic for Claude OAuth and supported direct upstreams.

api-keys.claude[].keys[].fingerprint-pro.description:
FingerprintProfile selects the Claude Code request fingerprint for this
credential on Anthropic Messages. Empty/default keeps the caller request
fingerprint and headers, including first-party api.anthropic.com API keys.
"claude-code-cli" opts official Anthropic API keys, custom gateways, and
delegated providers such as Kimi into the Claude Code OAuth CLI Messages
shape (OAuth betas, CCH signing, stable CLI identity) without treating the
credential as a real OAuth token for refresh/profile/runtime semantics.
CCH is a per-request hash and follows the native gate: it is emitted only on
api.anthropic.com and Vertex, so an opt-in on any other gateway sends the
billing block unsigned and cannot bust that gateway's prompt cache. Kimi
strips the attribution entirely by default and keeps it, unsigned, after an
explicit opt-in. count_tokens keeps the native model/messages/tools shape.
Recognized values are defined by NormalizeClaudeFingerprintProfile.

requests.tls-handshake-timeout-seconds.description:
TLSHandshakeTimeoutSeconds bounds upstream TLS handshakes made by the
shared uTLS client, in seconds. It applies to both the Claude Code
Anthropic transport and the Chrome ChatGPT/Codex transport; the
standard fallback transport is unaffected. It starts after TCP or
proxy connection establishment returns and does not bound dialing or
proxy CONNECT. Those uTLS paths use custom TLS dialing, for which Go
ignores http.Transport.TLSHandshakeTimeout, so a peer that accepts the
connection but never answers the ClientHello would otherwise block the
request indefinitely and request-retry could never engage. The bound
applies only during the TLS handshake and is removed once it succeeds,
so inference and long-running streams are unaffected. The default 0
disables the bound (previous behavior); negative values are treated as
0, and values beyond the representable duration range saturate.
requests.tls-handshake-timeout-seconds.template:
Maximum time, in seconds, for upstream TLS handshakes made by the shared built-in
uTLS client. It applies to both the Claude Code Anthropic transport and the Chrome
ChatGPT/Codex transport; the standard fallback transport is unaffected. The timer
starts after TCP or proxy connection establishment returns; it does not bound dialing
or proxy CONNECT. When the upstream path accepts the connection but never answers the
TLS ClientHello, the request would otherwise wait indefinitely and request-retry could
never engage. The bound applies only during the TLS handshake and is lifted once it
succeeds, so inference and long-running streams are never time-limited.
Set to 0 to disable (default).

MaxRetryCredentials defines the maximum number of different credentials to
try in each credential retry round.
Set to 0 or a negative value to keep trying all available credentials (legacy behavior).

Maximum number of different credentials to try in each credential retry round
after per-credential round filtering. Set to 0 to try all available
credentials. Credentials skipped by this cap still age with the global round,
so the cap does not guarantee a fixed number of actual retries per credential.

MaxRetryInterval defines the maximum positive cooldown wait, in seconds,
allowed before starting another credential retry round. A non-positive value
forbids positive cooldown waits; it does not disable same-round credential
failover or immediate additional rounds allowed by RequestRetry.
routing.retry.max-retry-interval.template:
Maximum cooldown wait in seconds between retry rounds.
Set to 0 or below to never wait for credential cooldown.
Retry rounds that need no wait remain controlled by request-retry.

routing.retry.request-retry.description:
RequestRetry defines the number of additional credential retry rounds after
the first round has exhausted its eligible credentials.
routing.retry.request-retry.template:
Number of additional credential retry rounds after the first round exhausts
its eligible credentials. Round 0 is the initial round; round r only admits
credentials whose effective request-retry is at least r. Explicit non-negative
credential/provider overrides take precedence; omitted or negative overrides
inherit this global value, and explicit 0 only admits round 0. New CPA nodes
send retry_round=0 for the initial round and increment it for additional rounds;
legacy dispatch methods omit the field and keep old semantics.
Additional rounds apply to HTTP 403, 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504 failures.
Individual credential/provider overrides take precedence; 0 disables additional
rounds, while an omitted or negative override inherits this global setting.

routing.session-affinity.description:
SessionAffinity enables universal session-sticky routing for all clients.
Explicit Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and pi session headers are preferred,
followed by prompt_cache_key, Responses conversation IDs, legacy body IDs,
execution or derived session identity, and the existing message-content hash fallback.
Automatic failover is always enabled when bound auth becomes unavailable.
routing.session-affinity.template:
weighted-round-robin uses each credential's integer weight (default 1, maximum 1,000,000).
Non-positive weights exclude the credential while this strategy is active.
For OAuth/file credentials, add a top-level numeric "weight" field to the auth JSON.
Enable universal session-sticky routing for all clients.
Explicit Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and pi session headers are preferred,
followed by prompt_cache_key, Responses conversation IDs, legacy body IDs,
execution or derived session identity, and the existing first-message hash fallback.
Automatic failover is always enabled when bound auth becomes unavailable.
An established binding outranks credential priority: once a session is bound, that
credential is kept even if a higher-priority credential recovers. Credential priority
still decides cold bindings, requests without a session, and post-failover rebinding.

routing.session-affinity-rebind-on.description:
SessionAffinityRebindOn controls which credential failures rebind an established session
to the failover credential.
Supported values:
  - "any" (default): any credential-attributed failure unbinds and rebinds on failover.
  - "quota": transient errors (408, 5xx, empty stream, buffer limit) fail over for that
    request only while keeping the session bound to its original credential; quota and
    auth errors (429, 401/402/403, 404/model support, invalid_grant) rebind as normal.
Ignored when SessionAffinity is false.
routing.session-affinity-rebind-on.template:
Controls which credential failures rebind an established session to the failover credential:
request only while keeping the session bound to its original credential; quota and auth
errors (429, 401/402/403, 404/model support, invalid_grant) rebind as normal.
Ignored when routing.session-affinity is false.

routing.session-affinity-subagents.description:
SessionAffinitySubagents controls whether subagents (child sessions with parent references)
inherit and bind to the parent's upstream credential across all providers (Claude, Codex,
Antigravity, Gemini), maximizing prompt and KV cache reuse.
When false, subagents are distributed across the credential pool via the fallback selector.
Default: true. Ignored when SessionAffinity is false.
routing.session-affinity-subagents.template:
When true (default), subagents (child sessions with parent references) inherit and bind
to the parent's upstream credential across all providers (Claude, Codex, Antigravity, Gemini),
for the same model, maximizing Prompt/KV Cache reuse and minimizing TTFT.
Guardian reviews (X-Openai-Subagent: guardian) may inherit across models from the
parent's most recent selection on the same real provider, if that credential is eligible.
This includes mixed-provider pools; result-driven TTL refreshes do not reorder selections.
Existing child bindings take precedence. Parent lookups do not extend the parent's TTL.
When false, subagents are distributed across the credential pool via the fallback selector
for maximum parallel concurrency.
Ignored when routing.session-affinity is false.

routing.session-affinity-ttl.description:
SessionAffinityTTL specifies how long session-to-auth bindings are retained.
Default: 1h. Accepts duration strings like "30m", "1h", "2h30m".
routing.session-affinity-ttl.template: How long session-to-auth bindings are retained. Default: 1h

routing.strategy.description:
Strategy selects the credential selection strategy.
Supported values: "round-robin" (default), "weighted-round-robin", "fill-first".

server.template: Listener, TLS, network discovery, and server operation.

server.commercial-mode.description: CommercialMode disables high-overhead request logging and HTTP middleware features to minimize per-request memory usage.
server.commercial-mode.template: When true, disable high-overhead request logging and HTTP middleware features to reduce per-request memory usage under high concurrency.

server.discovery.description: Discovery configures local network mDNS / DNS-SD service advertising.
server.discovery.template:
Enable local network mDNS / DNS-SD service discovery (RFC 6762 / RFC 6763).
When enabled, broadcasts _ai-gateway._tcp with API protocol subtypes on the local network.
TXT records follow draft-su-ai-gateway-discovery-00:
txtvers, path, tls, auth, protocols, auth_type, product, id, role
The TXT protocols list mirrors the advertised subtypes. Management endpoints are never advertised.
NOTE for Docker users: Link-local multicast (224.0.0.251) cannot cross default NAT bridge networks.
To broadcast across the physical LAN, run the container with host networking (--net=host / network_mode: host).

server.discovery.advertise-management.description:
AdvertiseManagement is deprecated and ignored. Management endpoints are never
advertised over DNS-SD; the field remains so existing config files still load.

server.discovery.auth-required.description: AuthRequired indicates whether authentication is required for client calls (default: true).

server.discovery.enabled.description: Enabled toggles mDNS service advertising on the local network (default: false).

server.discovery.interfaces.description: Interfaces specifies network interface filtering rules.

server.discovery.service-name.description: ServiceName is the optional custom instance name. When empty, defaults to CPA-<ShortID>.

server.discovery.service-type.description: ServiceType is the DNS-SD service type (default: _ai-gateway._tcp).

server.discovery.subtypes.description: Subtypes specifies DNS-SD API protocol subtypes to advertise (e.g. _responses, _messages, _generate-content).

server.github-token.description: GitHubToken is the global token for GitHub requests, taking precedence over GITHUB_TOKEN.
server.github-token.template:
Global token for GitHub requests (for example, release and asset downloads).
A non-empty config token takes precedence over the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable.
Leave empty to use GITHUB_TOKEN, or unauthenticated requests if neither is set.

server.host.description:
Host is the network host/interface on which the API server will bind.
Default is empty ("") to bind all interfaces (IPv4 + IPv6). Use "127.0.0.1" or "localhost" for local-only access.
server.host.template:
Server host/interface to bind to. Default is empty ("") to bind all interfaces (IPv4 + IPv6).
Use "127.0.0.1" or "localhost" to restrict access to local machine only.

server.max-request-body-bytes.description:
MaxRequestBodyBytes limits the size (in bytes) of incoming HTTP request bodies.
Values <= 0 disable the limit (default).
server.max-request-body-bytes.template:
Maximum allowed size (in bytes) for incoming HTTP request bodies.
Requests exceeding this limit are rejected with HTTP 413 Payload Too Large.
Default is 0 (disabled / no limit).

server.port.description: Port is the network port on which the API server will listen.

server.response-compression.description:
ResponseCompression controls negotiated compression of downstream HTTP responses.
It is configured under server.response-compression. Config.ServerResponseCompression
mirrors it for JSON and programmatic access; read the effective value via
Config.EffectiveResponseCompression.
server.response-compression.template:
Negotiated compression of downstream HTTP responses (including SSE streams).
Responses are compressed only when the client advertises zstd or gzip in
Accept-Encoding; WebSocket upgrades are never wrapped. Encoder memory is
retained for the lifetime of an open stream and depends on prior pool usage.

server.response-compression.enabled.description: Enabled defaults to true when unset.

server.response-compression.min-bytes.description: MinBytes defaults to 1024 when zero or negative.
server.response-compression.min-bytes.template: Non-streaming responses smaller than this many bytes are sent uncompressed.

server.tls.description: TLS config controls HTTPS server settings.
server.tls.template: TLS settings for HTTPS. When enabled, the server listens with the provided certificate and key.

server.tls.cert.description: Cert is the path to the TLS certificate file.

server.tls.key.description: Key is the path to the TLS private key file.

server.trusted-proxies.description:
TrustedProxies lists the IPs or CIDRs allowed to provide forwarded client IP headers.
The server applies this list at startup; changing it requires a restart.
server.trusted-proxies.template:
IP addresses or CIDRs of proxies allowed to supply forwarded client IP headers.
An empty list (the default) does not trust forwarded headers. Restart after changing this setting.

upstream.template: Shared upstream behavior applies to OAuth and API-key credentials.

upstream.claude.description:
ClaudeCode configures Claude Code compatibility behavior.

Claude configures provider-wide Claude request behavior.

upstream.claude.disable-claude-cloak-mod.description:
DisableClaudeCloakMode globally disables Claude request cloaking when true.
Cloaking disguises requests as the official Claude Code CLI and replaces the
system prompt. When true, every Claude credential defaults to no cloaking
("never"); a specific credential can still re-enable or override it via its own
cloak settings (the per claude-api-key "cloak" block, or a "cloak_mode" value in
the auth/OAuth token file). Default false preserves the per-client "auto" behavior.
upstream.claude.disable-claude-cloak-mod.template:
When true, disable Claude request cloaking on OAuth and API-key CLI profiles (the Claude Code CLI disguise and
system prompt replacement), so the original system prompt is passed through to Claude as-is.
Credential attributes and explicit per-key cloak modes override this shared default.
Default false keeps the per-client "auto" behavior (cloak only non-Claude-Code clients).
API-key overrides use api-keys.claude[].keys[].cloak.mode.

upstream.claude.disable-cloaking-model-l.description: DisableCloakingModelList disables model ID cloaking in Anthropic model list responses.
upstream.claude.disable-cloaking-model-l.template: When true, return original model IDs in Anthropic model list responses instead of cloaked IDs.

upstream.claude.header-defaults.description:
ClaudeHeaderDefaults configures default header values for Claude API requests.
These are used as fallbacks when the client does not send its own headers.

upstream.claude.model-level-cooling.description:
ModelLevelCooling scopes Claude quota cooldowns to the requested model
rather than cooling down the entire credential across all sibling models.
upstream.claude.model-level-cooling.template:
When true, scope quota cooldowns to the requested model rather than cooling down
the entire credential across all sibling models. Default is false.

upstream.claude.session-date-pin-days.description:
SessionDatePinDays retains the cloaked currentDate pin per session for
this many days, independently of continuity expiry and credential
switches. A nil value (unset) defaults to 7 days; an explicit 0 keeps
the continuity-scoped pin (1h lifetime).
upstream.claude.session-date-pin-days.template:
Days to retain the cloaked currentDate pin per session, so an idle gap or a credential
switch cannot re-anchor the date and invalidate earlier thinking signatures and the
prompt cache. Default 7; an explicit 0 keeps the continuity-scoped pin (1h lifetime).

upstream.claude.tool-search.description:
ToolSearch enables Codex client tool_search on Claude Responses routes:
Anthropic native tool search where the credential supports it, a pre-tool_search
translation elsewhere, and per-credential search advertising in the Codex
catalog. Default false keeps the translation that predates tool_search support.
upstream.claude.tool-search.template:
When true, enable Codex client tool_search on Claude Responses routes. Credentials on
api.anthropic.com (or keys with native-tool-search: true) receive it as Anthropic native
tool search (defer_loading + tool_reference), which keeps the prompt-cache prefix stable
across tool discoveries; other credentials fall back to the plain translation. The Codex
model catalog advertises supports_search_tool for a Claude model only when every
credential serving it supports native tool search.
Default false keeps the translation and catalog behavior that predate tool_search support.

upstream.codex.disable-codex-cloaking.description: DisableCodexCloaking disables forcing the official Codex identity headers on HTTP/SSE and WebSocket requests.
upstream.codex.disable-codex-cloaking.template: Disable forcing the official Codex User-Agent and Originator headers on HTTP/SSE and WebSocket requests.

upstream.codex.model-level-cooling.description:
ModelLevelCooling scopes Codex usage_limit_reached quota cooldowns to the requested model
rather than cooling down the entire credential across all sibling models.
upstream.codex.model-level-cooling.template:
When true, scope Codex usage_limit_reached quota cooldowns to the requested model rather
than cooling down the entire credential across all sibling models.
Default: false

upstream.codex.orphan-delegation-compati.description: OrphanDelegationCompatibility enables opt-in compatibility for orphan Codex delegation outputs.
upstream.codex.orphan-delegation-compati.template:
When true, enable opt-in compatibility for orphan Codex delegation outputs.
Converts orphan function_call_output items from codex_app/create_thread and
codex_app/send_message_to_thread (which lack a valid call_id or matching function_call)
into standard user messages across Responses and non-Codex protocols when the request
header contains X-Openai-Subagent: collab_spawn.

upstream.codex.response-steering.description:
ResponseSteering enables full-duplex Codex WebSockets, bound to one
upstream model/account/socket for their entire lifetime. Default is false.
upstream.codex.response-steering.template:
Experimental full-duplex Codex Responses WebSocket steering (default: false).
Keeps one upstream account/model per socket; accepted input is never replayed.

upstream.codex.stream-bootstrap-bufferin.description:
StreamBootstrapBuffering holds back the frames that arrive before generation starts, none of
which the client has seen anything from - the handshake (response.created, response.in_progress,
the websocket metadata frames), keepalive heartbeats, and the *.added announcements of an item
or part that is still empty - until the first generated event arrives. The upstream delivers
server_is_overloaded rejections inside an HTTP 200 stream right after those frames instead of
returning 503 on the wire, so buffering them keeps the downstream response headers uncommitted
long enough to retry on another credential. Trade-off: the response headers are delayed until
the upstream starts generating, which on a slow reasoning turn now means several heartbeat
intervals rather than one, and can trip client or reverse-proxy read timeouts. The hold is
bounded by a frame and a byte budget, not by wall-clock time, and neither budget is advanced
by a websocket peer that sends only control frames or by an upstream that never terminates an
SSE line. Only overload and rate-limit rejections fail over deliberately. A stream that ends
while the bootstrap is still holding ends the attempt rather than reaching the client, and
what follows is pre-existing but now far more likely, since the hold can span the whole
reasoning phase instead of ending at the first keepalive: a clean end with no terminal event
is request-scoped on SSE and stops there, while a websocket close or a transport error on
either transport is not, so the request may be retried on another credential.
Default is false.
upstream.codex.stream-bootstrap-bufferin.template:
Hold back the frames that carry nothing the client has seen - the handshake (response.created,
response.in_progress, the websocket metadata frames), keepalive heartbeats, and the *.added
announcements of an item or part that is still empty - until the upstream emits its first
generated event. Anything else, including a server-side tool item such as web_search_call and
any frame not on that list, releases the stream immediately. On the SSE transport the lines that
are not `data:` frames - comments, `event:` lines, blank separators - are held alongside them.
The hold is bounded by a frame budget and a 1 MiB byte budget, not by wall-clock time: an
upstream that trickles frames holds the response headers for as long as the client will wait.
Why: the upstream smuggles `server_is_overloaded` rejections *inside* an HTTP 200 stream,
right after those handshake events, instead of returning 503 on the wire. Buffering them
keeps the downstream response headers uncommitted long enough to transparently retry on
another credential. Only overload/rate-limit rejections trigger failover; every other terminal
failure is still delivered in-stream exactly as before. One pre-existing behaviour is worth
knowing, because this option makes the window it lives in much longer: if the stream ends while
the bootstrap is still holding, the attempt ends instead of the error reaching the client, and
whether another credential is then tried depends on how it ended. A clean end with no terminal
event is request-scoped on SSE, so nothing else is tried; a websocket close, or a transport error
such as a dropped connection on either transport, is not, so the request may be retried on
another credential. None of that is new, but before this option the hold ended at the first
keepalive, so it was rare; now it can span the whole reasoning phase.
Trade-off: response headers are delayed until generation starts. Because heartbeats are held
too, the delay now ends at the first generated token rather than at the first heartbeat. The
budget bounds how much is held, not how long: 48 SSE lines, which measures out as 15 heartbeats
of the three-line event:/data:/blank shape, 23 of a two-line ": keepalive" comment followed by
its blank separator, or 47 of a bare ": keepalive" with no separator - one short of the obvious
division, because the rejection frame's own event: line comes out of the same budget before its
line gets the round number instead. At a 10s upstream heartbeat that is 150s, 230s or 470s of
uncommitted response headers depending on the framing the upstream picks, all of it past nginx's
60s default proxy_read_timeout, so raise the timeouts in front of the proxy before enabling this.
Those seconds bound what the buffer holds, not when the response headers are committed. Headers
are committed on the first chunk the downstream translator actually produces, so for a format
that renders the handshake as nothing - Chat Completions and Gemini do - they stay uncommitted
past the budget, until the first generated token. That is not specific to the budget: any frame
that releases the buffer has always behaved this way.
The websocket transport spends the same 48 differently - one per message read, whether the loop
holds it or skips it, with no framing to divide by - so there it is 48 heartbeats, about 480s.
Two cases no budget covers: a websocket peer that sends only ping frames, which the library
answers inside the read call, leaving only the 5 minute websocket read deadline; and an upstream
that stops mid-line on SSE, where the scanner never returns and only the request context ends the
wait. Neither is made worse by this option - with it off the same stalled line stalls the
conductor instead, which waits on the same context - but a client-side request timeout, not
proxy_read_timeout, is what bounds them.
Default: false

upstream.codex.stream-bootstrap-timeout.description:
StreamBootstrapTimeout specifies an optional maximum duration to hold back uncommitted response
headers during bootstrap buffering before releasing the stream to the client.
Defaults to "0" (unlimited time, relying purely on the 48-frame and 1MB byte bounds).
When set (e.g. "20s"), the stream is released once the time ceiling is reached, avoiding
reverse-proxy timeouts (e.g. Nginx 60s proxy_read_timeout).
upstream.codex.stream-bootstrap-timeout.template:
Optional maximum duration to hold back uncommitted response headers during bootstrap buffering.
When set (e.g. "20s"), if the time ceiling is reached before the first generated token,
the stream is released to the client and further in-stream overloads are delivered rather
than failed over. This bounds how long trickled heartbeats or early empty frames can delay
response headers before streaming begins.
Recommendation: If your CPA is deployed behind a reverse proxy with a strict read timeout
(e.g. Nginx default proxy_read_timeout 60s or Cloudflare 100s timeout), setting this to "20s"
is strongly recommended to guarantee headers commit well before proxy timeouts while retaining
a comfortable 20s window to fail over early scheduling overloads.
Note: The timeout check is evaluated as upstream frames arrive; it never aborts the upstream
connection. Downstream headers are committed as soon as the downstream translator emits chunks
(for formats that render handshake/heartbeats, headers commit immediately on release; for
formats like Chat Completions and Gemini that render nothing until the first text token, headers
commit when that first token arrives).
When unset or set to "0", "0s", "none", "unlimited", "disabled", "off", or "never", no time ceiling
is applied, and buffering relies purely on the 48-frame and 1MB byte budget.
Default: "0" (unlimited)

upstream.codex.upstream-request-compress.description: UpstreamRequestCompression enables zstd request bodies for the ChatGPT Codex backend.
upstream.codex.upstream-request-compress.template:
Compress request bodies sent to the ChatGPT Codex backend with zstd,
mirroring the official Codex client. Applies only to OAuth credentials
targeting https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex (API-key credentials,
custom base URLs, and SIWC requests are never compressed). A 400/415
rejection is retried once with an uncompressed body. Default: false.

upstream.codex.upstream-request-compress.description: UpstreamRequestCompressionMinBytes defaults to 1024 when zero or negative.
upstream.codex.upstream-request-compress.template: Request bodies smaller than this many bytes are sent uncompressed.

upstream.codex.websocket-compression.description: WebsocketCompression controls upstream and downstream permessage-deflate; unset means enabled.
upstream.codex.websocket-compression.template:
Enable permessage-deflate compression on Codex WebSocket connections
(upstream and downstream) after negotiation. Default: true.
